Read bdmassault scsi.c:238-290 and modules/ilink scsi.c:304-358: in each copy scsi_read and scsi_write differ only in const and the 0/1 write flag passed to scsi_cmd_rw_sector (the ilink copy also has the same DEBUG_U64_2XU32 debug lines in both). ~26-line loop duplicated per copy; net ~20 per copy after one helper plus two thin wrappers.

scsi.c:30-41 repeats sbp2_driver.c:143-155's GetSystemTime / 64-bit subtract / SysClock2USec sequence (same in modules/ilink :144-156). warmup_interface is set only around the single scsi_warmup call in scsi_connect (bdmassault scsi.c:334-337, ilink :404-407), so the budget always applies. But the try count is not exactly redundant: with negligible command time the 300th try is checked after 299 delays (~29.9 s), one poll before the 30 s budget trips, and test_ilink_bd_reset.py:182 and test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py:193 assert turCalls <= 300 on a simulated clock. Dropping SCSI_READY_TRIES allows one more TEST UNIT READY and requires those test checks to change; the fix now says so.

corrected.fix: Make sbp2ElapsedUs non-static (declare it in scsi.h) and call it from scsiCommandBudget; drop SCSI_READY_TRIES and the tries counter, keeping the 30 s elapsed-time budget (it allows at most one more poll), and update the turCalls <= 300 checks in test_ilink_bd_reset.py and test_ilink_bd_assault_reset.py plus the scsi.c extraction in those tests so they supply the shared helper.

verdicts.note: part_driver.c:140 is the only assignment of part_connect_gpt; fs connect_bd is called only at bdm.c:184, after the sectorSize != 512 return at bdm.c:169-180. The device passed may be the cache device, but bd_cache.c:250 copies bd->sectorSize, and partition devices copy it at part_driver_gpt.c:171. So entriesPerSector is always 512/128 = 4 and the check at part_driver_gpt.c:69-74 cannot fire. git blame: lines 69-74 from 5fe47865 (2026-10-27).
